name: RoMa v2
plain: RoMa v2 (2025): dense matching between two photos of one scene from any viewpoints: where each pixel of the first image is in the second, and how sure the model is that it is visible there. Built on Meta's DINOv3. MIT code; the DINOv3 parts of the code and weights are under the DINOv3 licence.
summary: RoMa v2 (Edstedt, Nordström, Wadenbäck, Felsberg et al. 2025): dense feature matching between two images of any viewpoint. A frozen DINOv3 ViT-L/16 describes both images at a coarse square size, a multi-view ViT with alternating attention and a DPT head turn the global cosine matches into a coarse warp and an overlap logit, and convolutional refiners on VGG19-BN features (local correlation at strides 4, 2, 1) sharpen it, at the coarse size and again at a fine size. Returns, for every pixel of the first image, its position in the second (pixels) and the probability that it is visible there.

papers.title: RoMa v2: Harder Better Faster Denser Feature Matching

licence_notes: The checkpoint includes the DINOv3 ViT-L/16 weights, and net/dinov3.py and net/vit/ come from DINOv3: the DINOv3 License (Meta: attribution and conditions apply) covers those parts; read it before commercial use.
limitations: The precision matrices of the warp (upstream `precision_AB`) and upstream's sampling / keypoint helpers are not returned; tools/eval_matching.py has the MegaDepth-1500 sampling.
Both images are resized to squares (upstream's behaviour), whatever their aspect ratio.
task_io: Input: two RGB images of one scene. Output: for every pixel of the first image its position in the second (x, y in pixels) and a certainty that the pixel is visible in both.

variants.name: romav2

licence.training_note: Upstream README: a mix of wide-baseline matching datasets following UFM and MapAnything (MegaDepth and others; see the paper); none has a dataset entry here yet. The frozen DINOv3 descriptor was pretrained on LVD-1689M (not released).

variants.input_size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32

portable.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

kernels.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

original32.protocol: median of 5 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input, original code at the pinned commit, torch.no_grad; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls; float32
original32.note: upstream RoMaV2.match; local correlation: upstream's plain-torch path (no fused-local-corr)

original16.protocol: median of 5 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input, original code at the pinned commit, torch.no_grad; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls; bfloat16
original16.note: the authors' mixed-precision option (bfloat16); upstream RoMaV2.match; local correlation: upstream's plain-torch path (no fused-local-corr)

quality.title: MegaDepth-1500, relative pose AUC@5 / @10 / @20 degrees
quality.protocol: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling), OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors.

original16.note: upstream RoMaV2.match, enable_amp=True (bf16 autocast), local correlation: upstream's plain-torch fallback (fused-local-corr not installed)

quality.title: MegaDepth-1500, every 5th pair, relative pose AUC@5 / @10 / @20 degrees
quality.protocol: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling), OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors. The same 300 pairs for all modes, so float32 and bfloat16 compare pair for pair.

original16.note: upstream RoMaV2.match, enable_amp=True (bf16 autocast), local correlation: upstream's plain-torch fallback (fused-local-corr not installed)

original32.note: upstream RoMaV2.match, every autocast off, fp32, local correlation: upstream's plain-torch fallback (fused-local-corr not installed)

input.name: motorcycle
input.title: Motorcycle, Middlebury 2014 stereo (left and right view, downscaled 4x)

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 1.6e-05 vs the original. GPU, bfloat16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.0086 and p99 <= 0.032 (absolute error of the output `warp`).
